messages:
ava_sales: Hey team — acme fintech asked for an ISO applicability statement for the POC. They specifically want 1) which ISO controls we consider in-scope for hosted vs private, 2) a list of subprocessors and agreement clauses, and 3) data retention / deletion commitments for POC data. Can security confirm what we can provide for a sales POC?

nina_security: @ava_sales quick q — is the customer requesting the full LoA or just a short applicability matrix for the POC?

ava_sales: They said "short applicability matrix + evidence pointers" for procurement. They want to sign the NDA and start a 4‑week POC.

ben_se: For POC we usually offer hosted infra by default. If they need Private/VPC we can price that but lead time is longer. Does acme require data to remain in their VPC for the POC?

charles_cust: We prefer hosted but need assurance that PII will be deleted at POC end and subprocessors are listed. Also need to know which ISO controls Redwood manages vs which we must cover.

nina_security: OK — two pieces: control ownership mapping and evidence artifacts. For mapping we can produce a short table: control ID -> "Redwood", "Customer", or "Shared" with a 1‑line justification. Example entries: A.8.1.1 (Inventory) -> Shared (Redwood production asset inventory + customer app assets). A.10.1 (Cryptography) -> Redwood (kms + encryption in transit at rest).

mike_sre: I'll grab the control owners for infra controls and KV for encryption. NOTE: for hosted we rely on cloud provider subprocessors (AWS, GCS). Need to confirm list of third parties we can disclose for POC.

nina_security: For subprocessors we can provide the current list: [AWS, CloudSQL provider, Sentry, Datadog, Stripe] — but I will validate legal T&Cs around naming. Also need to include data processing addendum clause references.

ava_sales: Procurement asked whether we support contract language for subprocessor notifications (30d notice) and deletion SLA for POC data. What's the usual response?

nina_security: We can commit to deletion within 30 days of POC termination for hosted POC, documented in DPA appendix. For Private/VPC, deletion is customer-controlled but we can provide guidance and a verification script. Any stronger SLA requires legal signoff and an enterprise contract.

ben_se: Action items for SE: 1) capture POC host model (hosted vs private), 2) confirm retention window (default 30d deletion), 3) collect list of artifacts (policy doc, config snippets, SOC/ISO attestations). I'll draft a one‑page applicability matrix we can hand to procurement.

ava_sales: Timeline — procurement wants the matrix + evidence pointers before Monday (5 days). Feasible?

nina_security: I can put together the control ownership matrix and a pointer list to evidence (policy names + internal doc links). Will need Ben and Mike to confirm infra owners by EOD Friday.

mike_sre: I'll upload infra control notes to the internal evidence bucket and ping evidence-bot to generate a short package.

evidence-bot: Upload complete: s3://redwood-evidence/pkgs/1792345678-poc-evidence-v1.zip — includes: ISMS_policy_v2.pdf, infra-hardening-checklist.md, kms-usage-log-samples.txt

charles_cust: Thanks — can you include a statement on whether any backups of POC data are retained offsite and retention length? Need that for our risk team.

nina_security: Backups: for hosted POC only operational snapshots retained < 14 days. We will include that in the matrix (A.12.3 backups). For private deployments backups are customer-controlled.

ava_sales: Also procurement asked if any ISO controls are explicitly out-of-scope for this POC (e.g., physical security controls for customer office). We should call those out.

ben_se: We'll mark physical access controls and customer-managed IAM groups as out-of-scope for hosted POC where customer manages application auth.

nina_security: Good. I'll annotate the applicability matrix: InScope: A.5-A.14 core platform controls where Redwood is the operator. OutOfScope: physical access to customer premises, customer-owned application configs, customer user onboarding.

ava_sales: Pricing question from procurement — if they need Private/VPC for ISO boundaries, how do we quote? Ben?

ben_se: Standard: Private add-on = base + reserved capacity charge. For a 4‑week POC we can offer a reduced setup fee but not waive reserved throughput. I'll draft numbers and attach.

charles_cust: Good — can you include a sample clause that says Redwood will provide an "ISMS applicability statement" and an "evidence pointer package" within 5 business days of PO signature?

nina_security: We can commit to delivery timeline but legal needs to approve exact language. I'll prepare suggested wording: "Redwood will deliver an ISO 27001 applicability matrix and evidence pointer package within five (5) business days following receipt of a signed purchase order and NDA."

ava_sales: Perfect. Next steps summary please in thread so I can reply to procurement: who owns what and ETA.

ben_se: SE owns: produce matrix draft + pricing delta — ETA Monday COB.

nina_security: Security owns: finalize control ownership + evidence pointers + suggested clause — ETA Monday morning.

mike_sre: SRE owns: infra artifacts and confirm subprocessor list — ETA Friday EOD.

ava_sales: Thanks all. I'll loop procurement + attach POC scope draft once I have the matrix. :thumbsup:

charles_cust: Appreciate the fast turnaround :pray:
